title: Lesson 5 · The Pronoun
blurb: Personal & possessive pronouns, the three persons, possessives & apostrophes, and appositives.

items.prompt:
Which word is the pronoun?

“She lost the book.”
items.explain: “She” stands in place of a noun — it is the pronoun.

items.prompt:
Which word is the pronoun?

“Farmers sold it.”
items.explain: “it” stands for a noun — the pronoun.

items.prompt:
Which word is the pronoun?

“They sailed away.”
items.explain: “They” stands in place of a noun — the pronoun.

items.prompt:
Which word is the pronoun?

“Tom likes them.”
items.explain: “them” stands for a noun — the pronoun.

items.prompt:
Which word is the pronoun?

“Did you call?”
items.explain: “you” stands for the person spoken to — the pronoun.

items.prompt:
Which word is the pronoun?

“It rained hard.”
items.explain: “It” stands in place of a noun — the pronoun.

items.prompt:
Which word is the pronoun?

“Grandma saw him.”
items.explain: “him” stands for a noun — the pronoun.

items.prompt:
Which word is the pronoun?

“I won the race.”
items.explain: “I” stands for the speaker — the pronoun.

items.prompt:
Which person is this pronoun?

“I”
items.explain: “I” is the speaker — first person.

items.prompt:
Which person is this pronoun?

“you”
items.explain: “you” is the one spoken to — second person.

items.prompt:
Which person is this pronoun?

“he”
items.explain: “he” is the one spoken of — third person.

items.prompt:
Which person is this pronoun?

“we”
items.explain: “we” includes the speaker — first person.

items.prompt:
Which person is this pronoun?

“they”
items.explain: “they” are the ones spoken of — third person.

items.prompt:
Which person is this pronoun?

“she”
items.explain: “she” is the one spoken of — third person.

items.prompt:
Which person is this pronoun?

“it”
items.explain: “it” is the thing spoken of — third person.

items.prompt:
Which person is this pronoun?

“thou” (old form)
items.explain: “thou” is an older word for the one spoken to — second person.

items.prompt:
Which is the correct possessive?

the hat of John
items.explain: One owner — add ’s: John’s hat.

items.prompt:
Which is the correct possessive?

the horn of the ox
items.explain: One owner — add ’s: the ox’s horn.

items.prompt:
Which is the correct possessive?

the shoes of the children
items.explain: “children” does not end in s, so add ’s: the children’s shoes.

items.prompt:
Which is the correct possessive?

the car of the ladies
items.explain: More than one, ending in s — add just the apostrophe: the ladies’ car.

items.prompt:
Which is the correct possessive?

the coats of the boys
items.explain: More than one, ending in s — add just the apostrophe: the boys’ coats.

items.prompt:
Which is the correct possessive?

the shoes of the women
items.explain: “women” does not end in s, so add ’s: the women’s shoes.

items.prompt:
Which is the correct possessive?

the den of the fox
items.explain: One owner — add ’s: the fox’s den.

items.prompt:
Which is the correct possessive?

the nest of the birds (more than one)
items.explain: More than one, ending in s — add just the apostrophe: the birds’ nest.

items.prompt:
Is the possessive word a pronoun (stands alone) or an adjective (modifies a noun)?

“That book is mine.”
items.explain: “mine” stands alone for “my book” — a possessive pronoun.

items.prompt:
Is the possessive word a pronoun (stands alone) or an adjective (modifies a noun)?

“My book is here.”
items.explain: “My” leans on the noun “book” — a possessive adjective.

items.prompt:
Is the possessive word a pronoun (stands alone) or an adjective (modifies a noun)?

“Those apples are his.”
items.explain: “his” stands alone for “his apples” — a possessive pronoun.

items.prompt:
Is the possessive word a pronoun (stands alone) or an adjective (modifies a noun)?

“Her lesson is hard.”
items.explain: “Her” modifies the noun “lesson” — a possessive adjective.

items.prompt:
Is the possessive word a pronoun (stands alone) or an adjective (modifies a noun)?

“The victory is ours.”
items.explain: “ours” stands alone for “our victory” — a possessive pronoun.

items.prompt:
Is the possessive word a pronoun (stands alone) or an adjective (modifies a noun)?

“Your seat is there.”
items.explain: “Your” modifies the noun “seat” — a possessive adjective.

items.prompt:
Is the possessive word a pronoun (stands alone) or an adjective (modifies a noun)?

“Our house is large.”
items.explain: “Our” modifies the noun “house” — a possessive adjective.

items.prompt:
Is the possessive word a pronoun (stands alone) or an adjective (modifies a noun)?

“The garden is theirs.”
items.explain: “theirs” stands alone for “their garden” — a possessive pronoun.

items.prompt:
Which words are the appositive (they rename the noun)?

“Milton the poet was blind.”
items.explain: “the poet” is set beside “Milton” to name the same person — the appositive.

items.prompt:
Which words are the appositive (they rename the noun)?

“Nero, the cruel emperor, was hated.”
items.explain: “the cruel emperor” renames Nero — the appositive.

items.prompt:
Which words are the appositive (they rename the noun)?

“Mr. Whitcomb the lawyer is away.”
items.explain: “the lawyer” names the same person as Mr. Whitcomb — the appositive.

items.prompt:
Which words are the appositive (they rename the noun)?

“Washington, the capital, is on the Potomac.”
items.explain: “the capital” renames Washington — the appositive.

items.prompt:
Which words are the appositive (they rename the noun)?

“Stephenson, the engineer, lived in England.”
items.explain: “the engineer” renames Stephenson — the appositive.

items.prompt:
Which words are the appositive (they rename the noun)?

“My brother, a doctor, arrived.”
items.explain: “a doctor” names the same person as “my brother” — the appositive.
